explanations.answer: True
explanations.explanation: Not quite. Luke says they thought the kingdom of God would appear “imminently.” (Luke 19:11) That means any minute now, like someone standing at the oven door with the timer still running. Jesus was near Jerusalem, and that's the reason He told them this parable.

explanations.answer: False
explanations.explanation: Right, and here's the twist. Luke says they thought the kingdom of God would appear “imminently.” (Luke 19:11) That's not a long way off. That's checking the oven every ten seconds. Jesus was near Jerusalem, so He told them a parable.

explanations.answer: Do business with it
explanations.explanation: You've got it, baker. The man tells them, “Conduct business with this until I return,” (Luke 19:13) so the money is meant to go to work. Nobody gets a mina to just sit on it. Remember that line, because it matters when the servants come back.

explanations.answer: Keep it hidden safely
explanations.explanation: I see why it's tempting, since one servant does this later. But the man never tells anyone to hide it. His words are, “Conduct business with this until I return.” (Luke 19:13) That's about putting the money to work, not tucking it away like the last cookie in the box.

explanations.answer: Give it to the poor
explanations.explanation: That's a kind thought, but the text doesn't say it. The man tells his servants, “Conduct business with this until I return.” (Luke 19:13) The money is meant to be put to work while he's away. Nothing in the passage says he sends it to the poor.

explanations.answer: They don't want him ruling over them
explanations.explanation: That's it. The delegation says, “We do not want this man to rule over us.” (Luke 19:14) It's short and it's blunt. Nobody could mistake that message.

explanations.answer: They want him to hurry back home
explanations.explanation: Nope, it's the opposite. The text says his subjects hated him. Their message is, “We do not want this man to rule over us.” (Luke 19:14) Nobody is sending a hurry-home card here.

explanations.answer: They want his servants in charge
explanations.explanation: That's a creative guess, but the delegation never says it. The text gives their message in one line: “We do not want this man to rule over us.” (Luke 19:14) They say who they don't want, and that's all they say.

explanations.answer: True
explanations.explanation: Yes, ma'am, yes, sir. When he returns, he summons the servants he gave the money to, to find out what each one earned. It's report time. Think of the moment a boss says, "Let's see the numbers."

explanations.answer: False
explanations.explanation: This one is true, so let's fix it. When the man returns, he summons the servants he gave the money to. He wants to find out what each one earned. He gave them the money, so he checks on it.

explanations.answer: He was faithful in a very small matter
explanations.explanation: That's the reason, baker. The master says, “Well done, good servant! Because you have been faithful in a very small matter…” (Luke 19:17) One mina is the small matter here. The praise is for being faithful, and that's where the reward comes from.

explanations.answer: He kept the money safe for him
explanations.explanation: Close to the neighborhood, but not the house. Keeping the money safe is what a later servant does, and he doesn't get praised for it. This servant is praised because “you have been faithful in a very small matter.” (Luke 19:17) Faithful means he put the mina to work.

explanations.answer: He worked harder than the others
explanations.explanation: I get it, ten more minas looks like a lot of sweat. But the master never compares how hard anyone worked. He says, “Because you have been faithful in a very small matter…” (Luke 19:17) The reason he gives is faithfulness.

explanations.answer: Authority over ten cities
explanations.explanation: That's the one. The master says, “…you shall have authority over ten cities.” (Luke 19:17) Think about that jump. This servant started with one mina. Now he's looking at ten cities.

explanations.answer: A seat at the king's table
explanations.explanation: Sounds nice, but the master doesn't say that. His words are, “…you shall have authority over ten cities.” (Luke 19:17) The reward is authority, and it's counted in cities.

explanations.answer: Ten servants of his own
explanations.explanation: Ten is the right number, but the wrong thing. The ten minas are what the servant earned. The master's reward is, “…you shall have authority over ten cities.” (Luke 19:17) So it's cities, not servants.

explanations.answer: True
explanations.explanation: Not this time, baker. The second servant says, “Master, your mina has made five minas.” (Luke 19:18) Ten more minas was the first servant's report. Each servant gives his own number.

explanations.answer: False
explanations.explanation: Right. The second servant says, “Master, your mina has made five minas.” (Luke 19:18) That's five, not ten. And the master gives him authority over five cities, so his reward matches his report.

explanations.answer: True
explanations.explanation: Yes, he says so himself. The servant tells the master, “For I was afraid of you…” (Luke 19:21) He puts the mina in a cloth and names his fear as the reason. Those are his own words, and the master will use them in a moment.

explanations.answer: False
explanations.explanation: Let's go back to what he says. The servant tells the master, “For I was afraid of you, because you are a harsh man.” (Luke 19:21) He gives fear as his reason for laying the mina away in the cloth. That's right there in his own report.

explanations.answer: Put it in the bank to earn interest
explanations.explanation: That's it. The master asks, “Why then did you not deposit my money in the bank, and upon my return I could have collected it with interest?” (Luke 19:23) It's the simplest move there is. You hand it over, and it grows while you wait.

explanations.answer: Handed it to a neighbor to keep
explanations.explanation: A neighbor is a nice thought, but he never says it. The master's question is, “Why then did you not deposit my money in the bank…?” (Luke 19:23) The bank is the one simple thing he names.

explanations.answer: Traded it for a small piece of land
explanations.explanation: Land is a big commitment for one mina. The master points to something much simpler. He asks, “Why then did you not deposit my money in the bank, and upon my return I could have collected it with interest?” (Luke 19:23) So the answer is the bank.

explanations.answer: ten
explanations.explanation: Yes. The master says, “Take the mina from him and give it to the one who has ten minas.” (Luke 19:24) That's the first servant, the one whose mina produced ten more. The people nearby are surprised, because he already has plenty.

explanations.answer: five
explanations.explanation: Five is the second servant's number, so it's a fair guess. But the master says, “Take the mina from him and give it to the one who has ten minas.” (Luke 19:24) That points back to the first servant.

explanations.answer: two
explanations.explanation: Nobody in this story reports two minas. The master says, “Take the mina from him and give it to the one who has ten minas.” (Luke 19:24) The servants reported ten and five. The first one is the servant who gets this mina.

explanations.answer: Even what he has will be taken away
explanations.explanation: Yes. The master says, “…the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.” (Luke 19:26) That's exactly what just happened with the mina in the cloth. It's a hard line, but it's what he says.

explanations.answer: He will be given a fresh start
explanations.explanation: That's a hopeful guess, but it's not what the master says. His words are, “…the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.” (Luke 19:26) There's no fresh start in that line.

explanations.answer: He will be left as he is
explanations.explanation: It would be easier if he were just left alone, but the master says more. He says, “…the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.” (Luke 19:26) What he has is taken away.

explanations.answer: The enemies who didn't want him as king
explanations.explanation: Yes. These are the subjects from the delegation, who said, “We do not want this man to rule over us.” (Luke 19:14) The master calls them “these enemies of mine who were unwilling for me to rule over them.” (Luke 19:27) I think this is a heavy part of the parable, and it's worth slowing down for.

explanations.answer: The people of the distant country
explanations.explanation: The distant country is where the man went to lay claim to his kingship, and the last order isn't about the people there. It's about “these enemies of mine who were unwilling for me to rule over them.” (Luke 19:27) Those are the subjects who sent the delegation. It's a heavy order.

explanations.answer: The second servant with five minas
explanations.explanation: Not him. The second servant was given authority over five cities. The last order is about “these enemies of mine who were unwilling for me to rule over them.” (Luke 19:27) Those are the subjects who sent the delegation after him.
